verdict.headline: Visa-free tourism — check whether K-ETA applies to you.
verdict.sub: For visa-free entry, obtain K-ETA approval before boarding unless an exemption applies. A valid Korean visa or residence card has its own entry rules; K-ETA is not an extra visa requirement. Check your age and documents at k-eta.go.kr. K-ETA-eligible travelers aged 17 and under or 65 and over are exempt from mandatory K-ETA. This does not itself exempt them from the e-Arrival Card.

highlights.title: No visa for up to 90 days
highlights.body: Under the Korea–Thailand visa-waiver agreement, Thai passport holders enter Korea visa-free for short-term tourism and can stay up to 90 days. There is no tourist-visa application to file.

highlights.title: Check K-ETA eligibility and exemptions
highlights.body: For visa-free entry, obtain K-ETA approval before boarding unless an exemption applies. A valid Korean visa or residence card has its own entry rules; K-ETA is not an extra visa requirement. Check your age and documents at k-eta.go.kr. K-ETA-eligible travelers aged 17 and under or 65 and over are exempt from mandatory K-ETA. This does not itself exempt them from the e-Arrival Card.

highlights.title: Check the e-Arrival Card requirement
highlights.body: The e-Arrival Card is conditional. Valid K-ETA holders entering under K-ETA and valid Korean residence-card holders are exempt. A traveler entering with a visa may need the declaration even when also holding K-ETA. Other exceptions exist: use the official navigator for your documents and journey. This is an immigration declaration, separate from customs.

items.title: Confirm you're visa-free

items.title: Check K-ETA eligibility and exemptions
items.detail: For visa-free entry, obtain K-ETA approval before boarding unless an exemption applies. A valid Korean visa or residence card has its own entry rules; K-ETA is not an extra visa requirement. Check your age and documents at k-eta.go.kr. K-ETA-eligible travelers aged 17 and under or 65 and over are exempt from mandatory K-ETA. This does not itself exempt them from the e-Arrival Card. Apply early enough to receive approval before boarding. K-ETA assessment can take more than 72 hours; no approval time or entry is guaranteed. K-ETA costs KRW 10,000 plus the online payment fee and is non-refundable. Current approvals are valid for 3 years or until passport expiry, whichever comes first; this is not the allowed length of each stay.

items.q: Do Thai passport holders need a visa for Korea?
items.a: No — for short-term tourism, Thai passport holders enter Korea visa-free and can stay up to 90 days. You do not apply for any tourist visa.

items.q: Do I need a return or onward ticket to enter Korea?
items.a: Immigration can ask for proof of onward or return travel and where you'll be staying. Keep your ticket and accommodation details handy, even on a visa-free entry.
